# Plan a Realistic Week with AI

**Languages:** [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README_zh.md) · [日本語](README_ja.md) · [Deutsch](README_de.md) · [Français](README_fr.md) · [Español](README_es.md) · [한국어](README_ko.md) · [Português](README_pt.md) · [Русский](README_ru.md) · [العربية](README_ar.md)

Turn your available time and priorities into a weekly plan you can check and revise with AI.

[Start this course on AILesson](https://ailesson.io/courses/plan-a-realistic-week-with-ai)

A list of things to do can look reasonable until you try to place it around commitments that cannot move. AI can sort your notes and propose a timetable, but a neat table cannot create an extra evening or decide which promise you may break.

You will work through one practice week: an application to submit, a sharing session to prepare, a Saturday errand, and two lower-priority activities. You give AI the available windows and limits, inspect its proposal, then update the request when an evening disappears. The materials are prepared for this Course and contain no real personal data. The AI examples come from an actual production run and are presented as fixed responses for practice.

The first stage teaches you to separate facts, preferences and estimates so AI has a useful brief. The next stage shows how to check a proposed schedule and keep unfinished required work visible. In the last stage, you preserve the limits that still apply, review a revised allocation, and prepare the human follow-up that AI cannot approve for you.

You finish with a realistic proposal for the available time, an explicit record of a deadline that needs discussion, and a method you can reuse for a project, a study week or household tasks. Success here means knowing what fits and what needs a decision; it does not mean making every original wish fit or completing the scheduled work.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need to connect a calendar or use my own schedule?

No. The beginner path includes the complete practice notes and AI responses. You can follow the Course without a calendar connection or a separate AI account.

### Why does the example leave a required task unresolved?

The given time limits cannot accommodate every deadline. You practise recognizing that boundary and asking for a decision instead of accepting a schedule that silently changes your commitments.

### Can I use this approach for my own week?

Yes. Replace the practice notes with the time you actually control, your priorities and honest estimates. Confirm external opening times and deadlines yourself, and review the proposal before adding anything to your calendar.
